steps: The Grace Imperium fast-tracks the auction for the Philae Monolith's next decade of usage rights. Grand Inspector Matilda explains United Harvest's past and its current crisis, and officially asks for your help.
11:00, Venatio Month 8th, Gold District in Philae, Executive Office
"Early Bidding Opens for Philae Monolith Usage Rights"?! This is huge!
Whatcha reading, Iris?==W== "Monolith Usage Rights"? What does that even mean?
You know how there are "City Monoliths" managed by companies? Besides the "Wild" ones we usually climb?
Yeah. Only company employees or hired Trekkers get to touch those. Freelancers like us are stuck with the wild ones out in the boonies.
Technically ... we are employees. Of Boss Accord.
Hey Iris, does that mean we can climb the City Monoliths now?
Of course not! We don't have usage rights from the Grace Imperium, and we certainly haven't purchased any climbing permit from a licensed company.
Rights, permits... It's all gibberish to me.
Listen, Monoliths are divine gifts for the Novians.
And the Grace Imperium manages all Monoliths on behalf of the God of Grace.
They lease the City ones to companies, which require specific clearance to enter.
Being an employee alone isn't a free pass.
The Grace Imperium... The shop that sells Soul Stones? Are they really that big a deal?
They aren't just a shop! They're a massive conglomerate controlling the magical energy supply for all of Nova.
Since they hold the keys, they sell usage rights to companies, usually in ten-year contracts.
But after Darcia's stunt here in Philae, the Grace Imperium doubts United Harvest can manage the branch. So, they're auctioning the next ten-year contract early.
That auction process is what they call a "tender."
You make it sound so complicated. Basically, whoever throws the most Dorra at them wins, right?
It's not just about money. There are conditions.==W== Anyway... That's big company business. Small-time Trekkers like us wouldn't even be allowed in the building.
The familiar click of heels approaches the door as a cool, composed voice interrupts the conversation.
United Harvest's Philae branch must win this bid.==W== And to do that, we need to rely on the Boss's wisdom.
Boss. Everyone. Thank you for holding down the fort while I was gone.
Perfect timing.==W== I don't know the details yet, but this bidding war sounds like a headache...
I have a fair idea of the situation. Leave it to me, Boss.==W== In the meantime, I've brought a guest.
Boss, I've heard so much about you. It is an honor. I am Matilda, Grand Inspector for United Harvest.
My apologies for the sudden intrusion, but I must ask... Would you be willing to lend us a hand?
11:50, Venatio Month 8th, Gold District in Philae, Executive Office
Matilda and I sit opposite each other on the office sofas, leaving the executive seat empty.
Grand Inspector Matilda, thanks for uncovering the mastermind behind the banquet attack—and for making the trip to Philae. I know how tired you must be.
I'm happy to help if I can...
But you mentioned United Harvest? Honestly, I doubt someone like me has much to offer to a company of that size.
I meant what I said. As it stands, United Harvest needs the power you possess. But before I explain, I'd like you to hear a story.
Are you familiar with the name Samuel?
Rings a bell... I've definitely heard it before somewhere.
Trekkers' House. On the wall. The old man with the white beard.
Oh! He's the legendary Trekker who conquered a dozen Wild Monoliths. They say he's the reason there aren't any "uncharted Monoliths" left in Nova.
Precisely. Sixty years ago, after discovering the very last uncharted Monolith, he finally returned home to Philae.
Philae was a quiet farming town back then. Though it had a local Monolith...
The Monolith only yielded mediocre Artifacts. No company even bothered bidding for the rights to use it.
Samuel sank his life savings into it and took out a massive loan from Deepsea Finance.
He used a shell company to secure a ten-year lease through an old Trekker contact.
Folks thought he'd lost it. Why trade a peaceful retirement for a worthless Monolith?
He braved the Monolith alone and brought back Artifacts no one had ever seen and didn't even know how to use.
After demonstration, they finally understood—they were seed chambers, automated harvesters, and powder that helps crops thrive.
With those Artifacts, Samuel grew the finest wheat and vegetables in Philae.
Then, he simply gave those superior seeds to the local farmers.

He organized a fair-price system so farmers wouldn't undercut each other during a surplus, and no one would starve during a bad harvest. Slowly, food shortages gradually eased in cities around Philae.
Ten years later, he founded United Harvest using a Seal of Grace he'd been saving. Soon, affordable grains and produce were flowing down the river to every neighboring city.
The grain trade built Philae, turning a tiny settlement into the city you see today.
Wait, you mean ... the legendary Samuel founded United Harvest?!
That can't be right. Everything I've read says it started in New Orelian, bankrolled by a bunch of fruit merchants.
Sigh... History is cruel. Such a monumental legacy, quietly swept under the rug.
Nyx, Firenze. You both work for United Harvest. You must know Samuel's name.
Yeah. Actually, almost all United Harvest employees know about him.
But the official story is ... he was a terrible manager who nearly bankrupted the company.
Supposedly, the business only took off after the New Orelian merchants bailed him out, transforming United Harvest into a corporate giant.
Hmph. The Senate certainly works hard when it comes to revising history.
Samuel founded United Harvest with a single vision: affordable, quality bread for every person in Nova.
He poured his profits straight back into the land—expanding fields, building greenhouses, and improving seeds and irrigation.
But Firenze isn't entirely wrong. Five years in, unprecedented storms hit Philae. That year went down as one of the worst harvests in history.
The company's finances tanked. To save the farms and his workers, Samuel sold his shares to the New Orelian merchants and moved the headquarters there.
Flush with new cash, United Harvest spread its farms and storefronts to every city. Better yet, their food was cheap and top-tier.
Eventually, people stopped buying from anyone else. A natural market shift, I suppose.
Are we talking about the same company? That doesn't sound like the United Harvest we know at all.
Yeah. That business model sounds a lot like ... well, the ideal version of the company Firenze has been fighting for.
Undercut the market using deep pockets and endless supply. Sure, the customers win at first.
But once they're the only option left on the shelf...
Fast forward thirty years. United Harvest had become the largest grain and food supplier in all of Nova.
The Senate decided it was time to reap the harvest. Only they weren't after wheat—they wanted Dorra.
United Harvest gutted their product lines. Low-margin goods were axed, while top sellers saw their production costs slashed and retail prices hiked.
But wouldn't that ruin the flavor? They'd lose their customer base... Wait, no. They still have bustling shops in every city. Unless...
Wait, what? Am I the only one lost here? Boss, do you know what they are talking about?
The food industry demands massive, long-term investment for thin margins.
By the time United Harvest started hiking prices, they had a thirty-year head start. No ordinary farm could ever compete with roots that deep.
Once they secured a monopoly, they could inflate prices unsupervised. People had no choice but to buy from them.
Spot on. That is the reality of their monopoly.
People have to eat. As long as the bread isn't entirely inedible ... they'll keep buying it. Eventually, they'd even get used to the taste.
Tell me, my brilliant Boss... What do you make of United Harvest's success story?
Blinded by greed. They'll rot from the inside out eventually.
Nobody meant any harm, yet everyone will end up losing.
Boring. Spare me the corporate whitewashing.
Without a single competitor breathing down their neck, quality and fair pricing go out the window. They're free to strong-arm the market.
But people aren't fools. Whether it's the drop in quality or the soaring prices, public patience will run dry.
Keep this up, and it's only a matter of time before some new force—internal or external—tears them down.
Samuel had a noble vision, but he ignored the risks. As a result, the company became completely dependent on outside money.
Profit drives the economy. No matter who funded them, they were always destined for this outcome.
Customers naturally want the best products at the lowest prices. There's nothing wrong with that.
Samuel's dream matched those demands perfectly, creating a fragile cycle.
Nobody realized this setup would ultimately benefit no one.
But look at the outcome... The Senate is rolling in cash. Isn't that a happy ending? Sounds like a total win!
True. Though even the Senate must know they're bleeding the system dry.
Otherwise, nobody would resort to assassinations over the Philae branch's director seat.
United Harvest is clearly tearing itself apart.
Grand Inspector, you left out one crucial detail:==W== the Seal of Grace.
Sure, United Harvest expanded through massive production and deep pockets.
But you're likely the only agricultural firm in Nova holding a Seal of Grace.
A Seal of Grace lets you raise an army—but not every company chooses to do so.
Why would United Harvest, a food company, command a formidable private legion? Surely it isn't just for show. No. It must be because...
There are external forces standing in opposition to the company. Probably more than just a couple.
Meanwhile, your internal issues are boiling over. That assassination attempt at the banquet proves it.
You hit the mark. Without Samuel's guidance, United Harvest has been morphing into a monster over the decades, a greedy monster whose only concern is the Dorra in its own pockets.
The Senate fractured into warring factions. Nobody cares about the company's future anymore. Anyone who did was devoured by the rest long ago.
They don't even bother checking if the soldiers' wages are paid on time. They have no idea they're sitting on a massive powder keg.
So that's the mess you're dealing with.==W== Honestly, I'm even more certain now that there is not much I can do to help a giant like United Harvest.
My guild's a company, and so is United Harvest. Under the Seal of Grace's authority, we stand on equal footing. No one outranks anyone here.
The only real difference is that we're Trekkers.
But I don't see how our time in the field can be much help when it comes to running a corporate empire.
People rarely see their own worth. It seems like you haven't realized the true nature of the power you hold.
This may sound odd, but as proof... Gibel Corregio, the senator who orchestrated your assassination attempt, is already in custody.
You caught him?! But you just arrived in Philae. How'd you even pull that off so fast?
We have Boss to thank for that.
Good day, Grand Inspector Matilda. I've been expecting you.
Cosson? Thought you and your people were supposed to be retreating to Port Goldfinch.
That was the plan. But en route, I received a transmission from the Senate. They've given me a temporary mandate to represent the company at the Monolith bidding here in Philae.
Sounds like they really trust you.==W== Give it a few years, and you might be the talk of the Senate.
You flatter me. But clinging to power after a defeat is hardly "elegant." Once I return, I intend to resign my seat and focus on rebuilding the legion.
Rebuilding the legion? Are you sure? You've always obsessed over elegance, and life in the barracks is anything but.
If our military were truly "elegant," we wouldn't have suffered such a humiliating defeat over unpaid wages. The whole thing was a total farce.
Fair point. Let me make you a promise, then. To help you regain that "elegance," the Compliance Department will give you our full support.
I appreciate it.==W== But the main reason I waited was to hand this individual over to you.
You traitor! You're handing me over to Compliance? My friends in New Orelian will have your head for this, Cosson!
"Friends" in New Orelian, huh? Good to know. We'll just round them up right along with you.
Matilda?! What are you doing here?!
One more thing. Please tell the Boss and Lady Firenze that with you away from New Orelian, the Senate is moving fast. They're tabling an emergency motion today—
What are they thinking? If that branch closes, food supply will drop by ten percent. That's not just a shortage. It's a continental crisis.
They can't skim off the top in Philae, so they lose nothing killing it. Plus, they'll make a fortune hoarding the rest.==W== Typical inelegant behavior, wouldn't you say, Grand Inspector?
But the Senate backed Gibel. He was handpicked by them to run the Philae branch next.
Gibel, you orchestrated an assassination while under the Senate's wing. This is a slap in their face.==W== Are you planning to cross the New Orelian merchants?
That isn't the point, Grand Inspector. This is about what's elegant. Dragging everyone down for his own petty ambition... It's pathetic.
Besides, our main force only survived that massacre because the Boss commanded those Intelligent Plants with such ... undeniable elegance.
It's only right. When the Boss shows such consideration, we must respond with equal elegance.
Understood. You're putting a lot of faith in the Boss.==W== I'll make sure ==SEX== knows.
Just look at the people you've won over. Cosson who fought you, the Goodwind assassin who targeted you...
Firenze and Nyx who trust absolutely no one... Even Darcia holds you in high regard.
Boss, you possess something United Harvest lost long ago: the power to earn people's trust.
Please, help us. Let's save the Philae branch and keep Samuel's dream alive.
I was going to do that anyway.==W== Firenze is my ally, and I have friends in Philae. But more importantly—
Food is a necessity. Even a one-percent shortage can drive prices up until they're high enough for one percent of the population to starve. I can't just stand by and let that happen.
Our first priority now is figuring out how to halt the Senate's resolution... Do you have any strategy?
Honestly, I'm stuck. If I were in New Orelian, I could stop them... But they knew that and waited for me to leave before striking.
I'm in Philae now, and even with a witch's help, I can't get back to New Orelian in time. The Senate has me in checkmate. That's why I'm turning to you...
It's not checkmate yet. If you can make it to that meeting, you can turn the tide—correct?
Don't worry. I have a very reliable friend over in New Orelian.
